## About Hologic

Hologic helps women around the world live healthier lives.

We develop innovative medical technologies that effectively detect, diagnose and treat health
conditions and raise the standard of care globally.

We know women face unique health challenges at every stage of life, and we are passionate about
being a force for good.

Hologic is propelled by the passion and courage of our people to make a difference and innovate in
all we do. We believe everyone should feel welcomed, valued and heard, because great ideas come from
a diversity of views and experiences. We are proud to create opportunities for those who want to
grow their careers while making the world a better, healthier place.

# D-Dimer FS

## Emergency test for exclusion of thrombotic events

# Clinical relevance

During plasma coagulation soluble fibrin is generated. By degradation of cross-linked fibrin,
characteristic products called D-dimers are released. Increased D-dimer levels indicate the
activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis processes.** Low levels of D-dimer are mainly** **used
**to **exclude **venous thromboembolism (VTE) such as deep vein thrombosis of the leg (DVT) and
pulmonary embolism (PE).

## Diagnostic value of D-dimer
* D-Dimer may be determined **to exclude** a suspected **DVT or PE** with levels below a specific
  cut-off value
* Since neither a reference method nor reference material are available, clinical studies are
  mandatory** to define an assay-specific cut-off and calibrator values **
* Several studies support the use of a **cut-off value of 0.5 µg/mL FEU (fibrinogen equivalent
  unit)**
* If D-dimer levels are above cut-off value, imaging techniques such as sonograhpy or phlebography
  are mandatory for a definitive diagnosis of VTE
* Specificity for DVT is variable and depends on patient population; adjusted cut-offs were
  suggested for e.g. elderly patients or for individuals with cancer

We offer autism/AuDHD assessments for adults (18+)
completed by autistic and AuDHD psychologists with
expertise in high-masking presentations of autism.

### Screening

For some people, the autism screening provides the clarity they were seeking,
and so they may choose not to continue
to a formal diagnosis.

### + Formal diagnosis

your screening becomes the foundation of your full diagnostic assessment.

and disability accommodations.

  Learn how to identify the most common forms of hair loss.
  January 9, 2026
* [6 Common-to-Rare Infant Skin Conditions][63] Various skin disorders occur specifically in
  childhood. Although many of these are benign and self-limited, some require an extensive workup
  and close monitoring.
  January 2, 2026
* [Adult Brain Tumors: A Spreading Problem][64] Adult brain tumors constitute about 2% of all US
  cancers, and about one third of them are malignant. Although some are primary, most arise from
  metastases to the brain. Learn more about risk factors, diagnosis, and treatment of these lesions.
  December 29, 2025
* [Preventive Cardiology in Low-Access Communities][65] Social determinants of health play a
  significant role in the development of risk factors for CVD and are increasingly a target of
  consideration for preventive cardiology interventions.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, November 26, 2025
* [Community-Acquired Infections][66] Community-acquired infections are contracted outside of
  healthcare settings, significantly impacting daily life. They range from mild illnesses to severe
  diseases such as pneumonia and meningitis.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, November 13, 2025
* [Can't-Miss Gastrointestinal Diagnoses][67] Determining the exact cause of gastrointestinal
  symptoms can be challenging. Delays in diagnosis and treatment may result in serious
  complications, including abdominal catastrophes.
  November 13, 2025
* [Gout for the Holidays][68] Gout is the most common form of inflammatory arthritis. Once called
  the "disease of kings," gout can result from holiday-related overindulgence in certain foods and
  beverages.
  November 13, 2025
* [In-Flight Emergencies: Practical Medicine and Ethical Considerations][69] As a medical
  professional, what will you do when the airline asks for help for another passenger having a
  medical emergency? Are you prepared?
  Medscape Features Slideshows, November 3, 2025
* [Alcohol and Wellness: What's at Stake][70] Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a prevalent
  substance-abuse condition that affects every organ system.
  October 28, 2025
* [High-Risk ECGs][71] Rapid ECG interpretation is essential in the emergency medicine setting,
  often completed in under 30 seconds. Here, we review a series of ECGs with clinically relevant
  “can’t miss” diagnoses.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, October 21, 2025

AI agents handle drafts, code generation, research, and documentation. But there's a disconnect
that's slowing everything down: the place where your team thinks, plans, and refines their work
isn't the same place your agents can access it.

Your team and your agents should always be working from the same source of truth, a place where the
team sets direction, agents contribute, and everything stays aligned as ideas move from rough draft
to polished output ready to ship.

It's not just a collaboration tool for your team, but the shared context layer that keeps your team
and your agents in sync. Your team refines ideas in one place, agents pull from that same place, and
when agents contribute something back, it lands right where the team can review, edit, and build on
it together.

# WELCOME TO MAURYA LABS

# ABOUT

Maurya Labs was setup in the year 1998 by Dr A.K.Sinha in the city of Purnia. In the year 2004
Maurya Labs got the first 3 part hemoanalyzer and in 2007 the first fully automatic Biochemistry
Analyzer. Today Maurya Labs uses only 5 part fully automatic hemoanalyzers at all its labs. Dr
Anurag Mohan joined Maurya Labs in the year 2014 and is the main driving force in the deployment of
digital technology at the Lab.

 

# QUALITY

Maurya Labs has always been in the forefront of bringing the latest and most advanced technology in
the country in the field of Pathology. All our machines are closed systems delivering highly
accurate reports. Maurya Labs got NABL accreditation in the year 2012. In the last 26 years Maurya
Labs has earned the trust of doctors and patients for the timely delivery of test results and the
reliability of these results.

 

# NETWORK

Maurya Labs is now present in Purnia, Katihar, Araria and Madhepura. Maurya Labs provides pathology
services at multiple hospitals across the country by establishing a lab within the hospital. We have
more than 25 collection centres across Bihar. The logistics for sample movement are managed in such
a manner that we can delivery same day results for most of the tests anywhere in the country.

[urology surgery]

Kidney stones, ESWL

[ENT Treatments]

[leg vascular surgery]

Varicose Veins, Varicocele,

  storage infrastructure. With a compact design (only 7kg and an A4 footprint), the Poclight C5000

  emergency labs in disaster zones, it ensures accurate, on-site diagnosis without logistic
  barriers.

**About Us**

Specialists in rapid Point of Care diagnostic tests

Suresign Professional specializes in rapid point of care diagnostic tests & devices for the
healthcare sector. Our product range is designed for Point of Care testing in environments such as
GP practices, community pharmacies, emergency care clinics, out of hours services & hospital
clinics. We also supply products from reputable Point of Care diagnostic manufacturers under their
own brands. Suresign Professional are preferred suppliers to NHS Supply, NHS Scotland & HSE
R.O.I. Our products give healthcare professionals the ability to rapidly diagnose patients at the
Point of Care. This reduces the time to treatment initiation, resulting in better outcomes for the
patient at a reduced cost.

#### About

Suresign specializes in rapid point of care diagnostic tests and devices for the healthcare sector,
the product range includes urine analysis, family planning tests, as well as rapid diagnostic tests
to screen for drugs of abuse, infectious diseases and cancer markers.

#### What We Do

Suresign also supply a range of clinical laboratory tests & have a range of diagnostic devices to
monitor blood glucose, hemoglobin & coagulation.

#### The Brand

Award winning & preferred supplier to the NHS UK & HSE R.O.I. the Suresign Professional brand gives
healthcare professionals the potential to rapidly diagnose patients at the point of care, reducing
time to treatment initiation, resulting in better outcomes.

#### Disclaimer

Information provided on this site is for general use only. If you have any concerns about any aspect
of your health you should consult a healthcare professional for further medical advice.

### [Reference Ranges and What They Mean][91]

A reference range is a set of values that includes upper and lower limits of a lab test based on a
group of otherwise healthy people. By comparing your test results with reference values, you and
your health care provider can see if any of your test results fall outside the range of expected
values and gain clues to help identify possible conditions or diseases.

[Learn More][92]

## Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria Cause More Deaths than HIV or Malaria

A new global report found that more people died of infections caused by antibiotic-resistant
bacteria than HIV or malaria in 2019. Bacterial infections that don’t respond to antibiotic
treatment are a serious public health threat. Misuse and overuse of antibiotics have contributed to
this increasing worldwide problem.

[bacteria]
**Antibiotic Resistance in Bacteria**

Antibiotic resistance is when bacteria are able to survive and grow in the presence of one or more
antibiotics.

### Medical documents
* **MRI report**Explains the terms and key findings in your text MRI report
* **CT report**Breaks down the conclusions, areas of attention and radiologist's wording

* **Hospital discharge summary**A clear explanation of the diagnosis, tests, prescriptions and
  follow-up steps
* **Doctor's report**Turns medical language into a plain plan of questions and next steps
* **Prescriptions**Breaks down the regimen, the goal of each item and what to clarify with your
  doctor
* **Visit note**Structures complaints, examination findings, conclusions and recommendations
* **Test results**Cross-references text reports with lab values when they're uploaded together

### Blood tests
* **Complete blood count (CBC)**Assess overall health and a wide range of disorders
* **Comprehensive metabolic panel**Assess kidney and liver function, electrolyte and fluid balance
* **Lipid profile**Cholesterol levels to assess cardiovascular health
* **Thyroid function**TSH, T3, T4 — assessing the thyroid hormone profile
* **Hemoglobin A1c**A long-term measure of blood glucose in diabetes
* **Liver function**ALT, AST, bilirubin — markers related to liver health
* **PSA**Prostate health screening
* **C-reactive protein (CRP)**A marker of inflammatory activity in the body
* **Ferritin**Checking your body's iron stores

### Hormone tests
* **Testosterone**Reproductive and overall health in men and women
* **Estrogen**Assessing reproductive health in women
* **Progesterone**Fertility, pregnancy and cycle balance
* **Cortisol**The stress hormone and adrenal function
* **Insulin**Insulin production and diabetes control
* **Growth hormone**Tissue development and metabolism
* **DHEA-S**Assessing adrenal function
* **TSH**Regulation of thyroid hormones
* **LH / FSH**Reproductive hormone balance

* **Urinalysis**Screening

Why bother

## You have the labs. You don't have *clarity*.

You drew blood. You got back twelve numbers, three red flags, and the feeling that everything is
fine and everything is wrong at the same time. That's the part we rewrite.

01 · Anxiety with no anchor

### The "normal range" isn't *your* range.

Lab reference intervals are built for an averaged population. Your age, sex, lifestyle, history —
none of that fits inside the bracket.

**Before:** "FERRITIN: 28 ng/mL · LOW"
**After:** "second drop in a quarter for you — recheck in 8 weeks"
02 · Charts with no meaning

### Is the line going up *good* or bad?

Most services hand you a stock-ticker chart. But health isn't a portfolio, and "trending up" isn't
always a win.

**Before:** 12-point chart, "↑ +34%"
**After:** "B12 has risen four months running — supplements are working, you can step down the dose"
03 · Advice with no owner

### Recommendations from *nowhere*.

An AI can fire off 14 tips in two seconds. But who decided they fit you? Who's going to do them? Who
checks they worked?

**Before:** "drink 2L of water and move more"
**After:** an 8-week plan with one task per week, and the owner is you

job.

#### Drop the *PDF*

Any lab, any format. We pick out up to 340 markers. Nothing to type by hand.

03 · READ

#### A report in *sentences*

Not a table — a calm read. What matters, what waits, what to bring up with your doctor.

04 · PLAN

#### One thing *this week*

One task at a time. A vitamin, a recheck in 8 weeks, a consult. No checklist burnout.

one click.

# D-Dimer FS

## Emergency test for exclusion of thrombotic events

# Clinical relevance

During plasma coagulation soluble fibrin is generated. By degradation of cross-linked fibrin,
characteristic products called D-dimers are released. Increased D-dimer levels indicate the
activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis processes.** Low levels of D-dimer are mainly** **used
**to **exclude **venous thromboembolism (VTE) such as deep vein thrombosis of the leg (DVT) and
pulmonary embolism (PE).

## Diagnostic value of D-dimer
* D-Dimer may be determined **to exclude** a suspected **DVT or PE** with levels below a specific
  cut-off value
* Since neither a reference method nor reference material are available, clinical studies are
  mandatory** to define an assay-specific cut-off and calibrator values **
* Several studies support the use of a **cut-off value of 0.5 µg/mL FEU (fibrinogen equivalent
  unit)**
* If D-dimer levels are above cut-off value, imaging techniques such as sonograhpy or phlebography
  are mandatory for a definitive diagnosis of VTE
* Specificity for DVT is variable and depends on patient population; adjusted cut-offs were
  suggested for e.g. elderly patients or for individuals with cancer

# D-Dimer FS

## Emergency test for exclusion of thrombotic events

# Clinical relevance

During plasma coagulation soluble fibrin is generated. By degradation of cross-linked fibrin,
characteristic products called D-dimers are released. Increased D-dimer levels indicate the
activation of coagulation and fibrinolysis processes.** Low levels of D-dimer are mainly** **used
**to **exclude **venous thromboembolism (VTE) such as deep vein thrombosis of the leg (DVT) and
pulmonary embolism (PE).

## Diagnostic value of D-dimer
* D-Dimer may be determined **to exclude** a suspected **DVT or PE** with levels below a specific
  cut-off value
* Since neither a reference method nor reference material are available, clinical studies are
  mandatory** to define an assay-specific cut-off and calibrator values **
* Several studies support the use of a **cut-off value of 0.5 µg/mL FEU (fibrinogen equivalent
  unit)**
* If D-dimer levels are above cut-off value, imaging techniques such as sonograhpy or phlebography
  are mandatory for a definitive diagnosis of VTE
* Specificity for DVT is variable and depends on patient population; adjusted cut-offs were
  suggested for e.g. elderly patients or for individuals with cancer

  myocardial infarction have resulted in fewer mechanical complications. When they do occur, they
  are often catastrophic and require immediate surgical intervention.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, February 12, 2026
* [Pancreatic Cancer: Difficult Diagnosis, Ominous Outlook][58] Pancreatic cancer is a leading cause
  of cancer deaths in both men and women. Approximately 80% of all pancreatic cancers are
  adenocarcinomas, with only 2% of exocrine pancreatic tumors diagnosed as benign. Do you know how
  to distinguish the different histologic subtypes and initiate appropriate treatment?
  February 11, 2026
* [Thawing a Frozen Shoulder][59] Frozen shoulder, also known as adhesive capsulitis of the shoulder
  joint, is a common but sometimes difficult to treat condition. It often starts with shoulder pain
  and stiffness.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, February 4, 2026
* [Noise Pollution and Chronic Disease][60] Various forms of pollution, including noise, air, water,
  soil, and light, are linked to an increased risk of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, January 30, 2026
* [What the Eyes Tell You: 15 Abnormalities of the Lens][61] Lens abnormalities are associated with
  many conditions, and they can occur at all ages. How many of these have you seen?
  January 16, 2026
* [Hair Disorders: Finding the Root of the Problem][62] Hair loss, or alopecia, can be associated
  with a wide variety of conditions, from genetic to autoimmune to infectious to environmental.
  Learn how to identify the most common forms of hair loss.
  January 9, 2026
* [6 Common-to-Rare Infant Skin Conditions][63] Various skin disorders occur specifically in
  childhood. Although many of these are benign and self-limited, some require an extensive workup
  and close monitoring.
  January 2, 2026
* [Adult Brain Tumors: A Spreading Problem][64] Adult brain tumors constitute about 2% of all US
  cancers, and about one third of them are malignant. Although some are primary, most arise from
  metastases to the brain. Learn more about risk factors, diagnosis, and treatment of these lesions.
  December 29, 2025
* [Preventive Cardiology in Low-Access Communities][65] Social determinants of health play a
  significant role in the development of risk factors for CVD and are increasingly a target of
  consideration for preventive cardiology interventions.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, November 26, 2025
* [Community-Acquired Infections][66] Community-acquired infections are contracted outside of
  healthcare settings, significantly impacting daily life. They range from mild illnesses to severe
  diseases such as pneumonia and meningitis.
  Medscape Features Slideshows, November 13, 2025
* [Can't-Miss Gastrointestinal Diagnoses][67] Determining the exact cause of gastrointestinal
  symptoms can be challenging. Delays in diagnosis and treatment may result in serious
  complications, including abdominal catastrophes.
  November 13, 2025
* [Gout for the Holidays][68] Gout is the most common form of inflammatory arthritis. Once called
  the "disease of kings," gout can result from holiday-related overindulgence in certain foods and
  beverages.
  November 13, 2025
* [In-Flight Emergencies: Practical Medicine and Ethical Considerations][69] As a medical
  professional, what will you do when the airline asks for help for another passenger having a
  medical emergency? Are you prepared?
  Medscape Features Slideshows, November 3, 2025
* [Alcohol and Wellness: What's at Stake][70] Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a prevalent
  substance-abuse condition that affects every organ system.
  October 28, 2025
* [High-Risk ECGs][71] Rapid ECG interpretation is essential in the emergency medicine setting,
  often completed in under 30 seconds. Here, we review a series of ECGs with clinically relevant
  “can’t miss” diagnoses.

## Your team has ideas,

## HackMD brings them together

###### Teams are shipping faster than ever

AI agents handle drafts, code generation, research, and documentation. But there's a disconnect
that's slowing everything down: the place where your team thinks, plans, and refines their work
isn't the same place your agents can access it.

###### What's missing is a shared layer

Your team and your agents should always be working from the same source of truth, a place where the
team sets direction, agents contribute, and everything stays aligned as ideas move from rough draft
to polished output ready to ship.

###### That's where HackMD comes in

It's not just a collaboration tool for your team, but the shared context layer that keeps your team
and your agents in sync. Your team refines ideas in one place, agents pull from that same place, and
when agents contribute something back, it lands right where the team can review, edit, and build on
it together.

# WELCOME TO MAURYA LABS

# ABOUT

Maurya Labs was setup in the year 1998 by Dr A.K.Sinha in the city of Purnia. In the year 2004
Maurya Labs got the first 3 part hemoanalyzer and in 2007 the first fully automatic Biochemistry
Analyzer. Today Maurya Labs uses only 5 part fully automatic hemoanalyzers at all its labs. Dr
Anurag Mohan joined Maurya Labs in the year 2014 and is the main driving force in the deployment of
digital technology at the Lab.

 

# QUALITY

Maurya Labs has always been in the forefront of bringing the latest and most advanced technology in
the country in the field of Pathology. All our machines are closed systems delivering highly
accurate reports. Maurya Labs got NABL accreditation in the year 2012. In the last 26 years Maurya
Labs has earned the trust of doctors and patients for the timely delivery of test results and the
reliability of these results.

 

# NETWORK

Maurya Labs is now present in Purnia, Katihar, Araria and Madhepura. Maurya Labs provides pathology
services at multiple hospitals across the country by establishing a lab within the hospital. We have
more than 25 collection centres across Bihar. The logistics for sample movement are managed in such
a manner that we can delivery same day results for most of the tests anywhere in the country.

**About Us**

Specialists in rapid Point of Care diagnostic tests

Suresign Professional specializes in rapid point of care diagnostic tests & devices for the
healthcare sector. Our product range is designed for Point of Care testing in environments such as
GP practices, community pharmacies, emergency care clinics, out of hours services & hospital
clinics. We also supply products from reputable Point of Care diagnostic manufacturers under their
own brands. Suresign Professional are preferred suppliers to NHS Supply, NHS Scotland & HSE
R.O.I. Our products give healthcare professionals the ability to rapidly diagnose patients at the
Point of Care. This reduces the time to treatment initiation, resulting in better outcomes for the
patient at a reduced cost.

#### About

Suresign specializes in rapid point of care diagnostic tests and devices for the healthcare sector,
the product range includes urine analysis, family planning tests, as well as rapid diagnostic tests
to screen for drugs of abuse, infectious diseases and cancer markers.

#### What We Do

Suresign also supply a range of clinical laboratory tests & have a range of diagnostic devices to
monitor blood glucose, hemoglobin & coagulation.

#### The Brand

Award winning & preferred supplier to the NHS UK & HSE R.O.I. the Suresign Professional brand gives
healthcare professionals the potential to rapidly diagnose patients at the point of care, reducing
time to treatment initiation, resulting in better outcomes.

# Understand your lab tests, understand your health

At Testing.com, we help consumers advocate for their health by providing them with learning guides
and products that make lab testing accessible, convenient and affordable.

Hundreds of easy-to-read lab testing guides. Confidential, secure and convenient online lab test
ordering powered by direct access to our laboratory partners. Compassionate customer support. We
combine expert-reviewed lab test information with access to hundreds of in-lab and at-home tests.

Testing.com is supported by readers and we may also earn commissions through products purchased
using links on this page. You can read more about how we make money [here][50].

## How it Works

### It’s all about the data.

Lab testing provides the data you need to build and maintain a care plan that is as custom and
convenient as possible. Read over 400 expert-reviewed lab test guides to better understand what each
test measures, how it’s used, when you might need a particular test, and more.

[View Testing Guides][52]
[How it Works Image 1]

### Turn information into action.

If you need a test, order lab tests and at-home test kits through our laboratory partners directly.

### [Reference Ranges and What They Mean][91]

A reference range is a set of values that includes upper and lower limits of a lab test based on a
group of otherwise healthy people. By comparing your test results with reference values, you and
your health care provider can see if any of your test results fall outside the range of expected
values and gain clues to help identify possible conditions or diseases.

[Learn More][92]

## Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria Cause More Deaths than HIV or Malaria

A new global report found that more people died of infections caused by antibiotic-resistant
bacteria than HIV or malaria in 2019. Bacterial infections that don’t respond to antibiotic
treatment are a serious public health threat. Misuse and overuse of antibiotics have contributed to
this increasing worldwide problem.

Antibiotic resistance is when bacteria are able to survive and grow in the presence of one or more

### Medical documents
* **MRI report**Explains the terms and key findings in your text MRI report

* **Hospital discharge summary**A clear explanation of the diagnosis, tests, prescriptions and
  follow-up steps
* **Doctor's report**Turns medical language into a plain plan of questions and next steps
* **Prescriptions**Breaks down the regimen, the goal of each item and what to clarify with your
  doctor
* **Visit note**Structures complaints, examination findings, conclusions and recommendations
* **Test results**Cross-references text reports with lab values when they're uploaded together

### Blood tests
* **Complete blood count (CBC)**Assess overall health and a wide range of disorders
* **Comprehensive metabolic panel**Assess kidney and liver function, electrolyte and fluid balance
* **Lipid profile**Cholesterol levels to assess cardiovascular health
* **Thyroid function**TSH, T3, T4 — assessing the thyroid hormone profile
* **Hemoglobin A1c**A long-term measure of blood glucose in diabetes
* **Liver function**ALT, AST, bilirubin — markers related to liver health
* **PSA**Prostate health screening
* **C-reactive protein (CRP)**A marker of inflammatory activity in the body
* **Ferritin**Checking your body's iron stores

### Hormone tests
* **Testosterone**Reproductive and overall health in men and women
* **Estrogen**Assessing reproductive health in women
* **Progesterone**Fertility, pregnancy and cycle balance
* **Cortisol**The stress hormone and adrenal function
* **Insulin**Insulin production and diabetes control
* **Growth hormone**Tissue development and metabolism
* **DHEA-S**Assessing adrenal function
* **TSH**Regulation of thyroid hormones
* **LH / FSH**Reproductive hormone balance

* **Urinalysis**Screening

Why bother

## You have the labs. You don't have *clarity*.

You drew blood. You got back twelve numbers, three red flags, and the feeling that everything is
fine and everything is wrong at the same time. That's the part we rewrite.

01 · Anxiety with no anchor

### The "normal range" isn't *your* range.

Lab reference intervals are built for an averaged population. Your age, sex, lifestyle, history —
none of that fits inside the bracket.

**Before:** "FERRITIN: 28 ng/mL · LOW"
**After:** "second drop in a quarter for you — recheck in 8 weeks"
02 · Charts with no meaning

### Is the line going up *good* or bad?

Most services hand you a stock-ticker chart. But health isn't a portfolio, and "trending up" isn't
always a win.

**Before:** 12-point chart, "↑ +34%"
**After:** "B12 has risen four months running — supplements are working, you can step down the dose"
03 · Advice with no owner

### Recommendations from *nowhere*.

An AI can fire off 14 tips in two seconds. But who decided they fit you? Who's going to do them? Who
checks they worked?

**Before:** "drink 2L of water and move more"
**After:** an 8-week plan with one task per week, and the owner is you
